Yes, I've seen this too.  A simple example Nextjs project that builds in standalong mode works on it's own.  But when run from inside an pnpm mono repo, the build app doesn't work.

It's not only that the standalone mode misses some dependency modules, it seems to just copy a few files from withing those modules.

Could it be that it's getting confused by pnpm's use of symlinks.  Or could it be something else?

My colleague @millsp previously connected this to another issue https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/42651, where he posted a bit of an analysis as well: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/42651#issuecomment-1399053794 

Based on that he also came up with a workaround: `rm -fr .next/standalone/node_modules/next`. After running this command, I can successfully start and use the app.

@janpio that just removes the broken copy of 'next' from the standalone folder. So when you run the app, it will find 'next' in the node_modules of the parent folder.  If you were to copy the 'standalone' folder out to somewhere else on the filessystem or another machine. Then it wouldn't work.  Right?

Yes, that's right. I was deleting this folder just for the sake of doing a local reproduction with `next` + `prisma`. I don't think it would deploy correctly, indeed. Hopefully this will highlight the problem. From what I have seen, only the server file is copied but not the rest of the files that are needed. I could reproduce with `pnpm` and `npm` workspaces.

I did some changes to your repo:
- `scripts/recreate.sh`
```sh
#!/bin/bash

cd ./source/apps/app-collection/api-routes-app
pnpm run build
mkdir .next/standalone/source/apps/app-collection/api-routes-app/.next/static
cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/source/apps/app-collection/api-routes-app/.next
node .next/standalone/source/apps/app-collection/api-routes-app/server.js
```
- Root `pnpm-lock.yaml`:
```yaml
packages:
  # all packages in subdirs of apps/
  - 'source/apps/**'
  # all packages in direct subdirs of packages/
  - 'packages/**'
```
- Your `next.config.js`:
```js
const { join } = require('path');

/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
module.exports = {
  output: 'standalone',
  experimental: {
    outputFileTracingRoot: join(__dirname, "../../../..")
  }
}
```
And deleted `pnpm-lock.yaml` in other folders, since those aren't needed. Then I tried to build and it worked just fine. Please see the [caveats](https://nextjs.org/docs/advanced-features/output-file-tracing#caveats) section here, it says that you need to use `experimental.outputFileTracingRoot` in monorepos. Hope this helps :)

I'm debugging this issue right now for my project, I've found that the issue does not occur consistently on all machines.

One one machine, after I run `next build`, my `.next/standalone/node_modules/next/dist/server` only contains these files:

```
drwxrwxr-x 2 runner runner  4096 Feb 16 07:43 .
drwxrwxr-x 8 runner runner  4096 Feb 16 07:43 ..
-rw-rw-r-- 1 runner runner   708 Feb 16 07:43 get-page-files.js
-rw-rw-r-- 1 runner runner   698 Feb 16 07:43 htmlescape.js
-rw-rw-r-- 1 runner runner 71950 Feb 16 07:43 next-server.js
-rw-rw-r-- 1 runner runner   681 Feb 16 07:43 utils.js
```
So it's clearly missing `initialize-require-hook` for example and thus next fails to start.

However, on a second machine, with the exact same repo and following the exact same build steps, the `.next/standalone/node_modules/next/dist/server` contains much more files (including `initialize-require-hook.js`), and the next server.js starts without issues.

Both machines are ARM based, both are running the exact same version of node (v18.13.0), so I'm still trying to figure out what the actual difference is and why one machine is producing different results.

issue.title: Refactor require hooks
issue.body:
Same purpose as #48297, but without the React channel branching logic to make it easier to land. Since we have #48478 reverted, we only need to consider `pages` and `app` inside the require hook.

> This PR aims to improve the current require hook by implementing two key changes. Firstly, it ensures that the initialization occurs at the top of the module level for correctness. Secondly, we now set the NEXT_PREBUNDLED_REACT environment variable at the process level to ensure that we don't mix the two types of rendering processes and we always resolve the correct React package.
>
> These improvements are made possible by the changes introduced in PR https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/47857.
> 
> Closes [NEXT-231](https://linear.app/vercel/issue/NEXT-231).

This will likely fix #45258 too.

I ran into the same problem and could _workaround_ the issue by adding a `.npmrc` to my monorepo-root.

```
shared-workspace-lockfile=false
```

That alone won't be enough if you have specified `outputFileTracingRoot` in your Next config.
